headline: High-risk workspace and tool overlap: ECC can write/egress while the other profile is a docs-only prompt resource, creating default conflict and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a docs-only prompt-engineering repository with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject into ECC by itself. Profile B can read/write files and use MCP, so if an operator manually copies A’s content into B’s workspace, prompt injection becomes possible, but that bridge is unusual and not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from agent_a docs into agent_b prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is configured to parse untrusted file content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Keep agent_a content out of agent_b instruction channels.
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted files in agent_b.
Use a fixed prompt template that separates data from instructions.
Review copied snippets before pasting into agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no data classes touched, but agent B touches session summaries, git history, code, and security findings and can write files and egress to allowlisted APIs. If A’s prompt resources are placed in B’s shared workspace, B can upload or expose them through its normal tooling. The pairwise leakage path exists in default ECC workflows, though A itself is not a data source.
conditions: IF agent_a materials are stored in agent_b-accessible files, B can read them.
IF agent_b sends workspace contents to allowlisted APIs, copied A content may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Store agent_a materials outside agent_b workspaces.
Restrict agent_b egress to the minimum allowlist.
Separate credentials and profiles for each agent.
Audit files under ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc before use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with OS permissions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write capabilities, but agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. Because B’s concurrency model explicitly warns about shared state across instances, default multi-instance use can overwrite shared files. Uncertainty about A’s lack of runtime isolation does not reduce the conflict risk; it increases it because no blocking mechanism is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF agent_b runs alongside another instance using the same root, shared files can be overwritten.
IF agent_b modifies git state in a shared repo, concurrent edits can conflict.
mitigations: Use separate roots for each agent instance.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same repo.
Back up git state before running agent_b.
Limit agent_b to read-only mode for shared repos.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a prompt-engineering resource, so its outputs are likely to be reused as guidance. Agent B’s skills are the primary workflow surface and it can act on inputs with shell, git, and browser tools. That makes a plausible cascade where A’s guidance is treated as authoritative by B, but the pair is not documented as an automated handoff, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-derived prompts or instructions without verification, errors can propagate.
IF agent_b uses A’s guidance to drive shell or browser actions, downstream mistakes can compound.
mitigations: Require human review before executing A-derived instructions in B.
Add a verification step for facts before tool use.
Keep A as reference material, not an action source.
Log and diff B’s planned actions against source guidance.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation for imported instructions.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class is identified for agent A, while agent B explicitly handles session summaries, metrics, git history, and security findings. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a small compliance gap is plausible if A materials are copied into B’s retained session data. The other agent is cited because the risk arises only when B stores or retains imported content.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive content from agent_a is copied into agent_b session summaries or retained files, retention policy mismatch may occur.
IF agent_b retains imported content longer than intended, deletion/export handling can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive A content into B session summaries.
Shorten B retention settings for imported material.
Review retained files in ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc.
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows from B.
requires-engineering: add per-data-class retention controls.
